candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And now my son Methuselah, [I will recount these things to thee and write them down for thee], and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father's hand... And now, my children, listen to me, love righteousness and walk therein; for the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptation, but the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish' — the two-paths exhortation. Tewahedo catechetical tradition uses the two-paths formula (preserved also in Didache 1-6) as foundational moral instruction for the catechumen.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression and lay deceit as a foundation; for they shall be suddenly overthrown, and they shall have no peace' — first woe oracle. Tewahedo prophetic-homily tradition reads the Enochic woe oracles as direct precedent for the Lukan woe oracles (Lk 6:24-26) and Jacobean injustice-woes (Jas 5:1-6) — the verbal pattern is continuous: woe + the deed condemned + the future judgment.
